description: What the DigitalOcean account holds and whether any of it is unhealthy. Start here, then follow the dropdown at the top for detail.

panels.description: Account flags straight from the DigitalOcean account endpoint. An account that is not active cannot create resources. Needs --collector.account.
panels.title: Account

panels.description: How many of each resource the account holds right now. A missing number means the collector for that resource is switched off, not that the count is zero -- check the Exporter dashboard.
panels.title: Inventory

panels.description: Reserved IPs assigned to no droplet. DigitalOcean bills a reserved IP only while it serves nothing, so anything above zero is money spent on an address a destroyed droplet left behind. DigitalOceanReservedIPUnassigned alerts on it after a day. Needs --collector.reservedips.
panels.title: Idle reserved IPs

panels.description: Anything DigitalOcean does not report as running. Every number should be zero. 'Collectors failing' counts exporter collectors whose last refresh errored -- their other numbers on these dashboards are then stale, not wrong.
panels.title: Unhealthy

panels.description: Usage as a fraction of the per-account limit DigitalOcean enforces. These are soft limits: support raises them on request, but hitting one makes the next create call fail. Needs --collector.limits.
panels.title: Account limits used

panels.description: Every managed database cluster on the account. 'Online' is 1 when the cluster is serving. Needs --collector.databases.

targets.expr: max by (id, name, region, engine, version, size) (digitalocean_database_status{job=~"$job"})

panels.title: Managed databases

panels.description: Age of the newest backup of each managed database cluster. DigitalOcean backs clusters up daily, so anything past 36 hours means a missed backup and is what DigitalOceanDatabaseBackupStale fires on. Engines without backups never appear here. Needs --collector.databases.details.
panels.title: Database backup age

panels.description: Read-only replicas per managed database cluster. A cluster whose engine offers no replicas reports 0. Needs --collector.databases.details.
panels.title: Database replicas

panels.description: Every read-only replica and the status it reports. The region is the replica's own, which may differ from its cluster's. Needs --collector.databases.details.
panels.title: Database replica status

panels.description: CDN endpoints and how long they cache an object. A custom domain with an empty certificate is served over the DigitalOcean domain only. Needs --collector.cdn.

targets.expr: max by (id, cdn_endpoint, origin, custom_domain, certificate_id) (label_replace(label_replace(digitalocean_cdn_endpoint_info{job=~"$job"}, "cdn_endpoint", "$1", "endpoint", "(.+)"), "cdn_endpoint", "$1", "exported_endpoint", "(.+)"))

panels.title: CDN endpoints

panels.description: DNS zones hosted by DigitalOcean and the default TTL of each zone. Needs --collector.domains.
panels.title: DNS domains

list.description: The Prometheus instance that scrapes digitalocean_exporter.
list.label: Data source
list.name: datasource

list.description: Prometheus job of the exporter. Pick a single job when you run one exporter per DigitalOcean account and want to look at just one of them.
list.label: Job
list.name: job

title: DigitalOcean / Overview
